title: Saans scene
description:
A room as DEFINED, not as measured. Everything in this file is SCENE data: somebody typed it, imported it from a LiDAR scan, or measured it with a tape. None of it comes from WiFi. ESP32 CSI at 20 MHz on a single antenna cannot measure room dimensions and cannot recognise furniture (docs/CAPABILITY_LIMITS.md), so a viewer must label these numbers SCENE and never attribute them to the radio.

AXES. x is width_m, y is depth_m, z is height_m, origin at a floor corner, metres throughout (every field says so in its name). y is the second HORIZONTAL axis of the floor plan; z is ELEVATION. This matters because wifisense.localize.geometry.Room calls its second horizontal axis `height_m`: converting a scene to that type maps scene depth_m -> Room.height_m and drops the scene's elevation. Getting that backwards silently rotates the room, so both loaders do the mapping in one documented place (wifisense/scene.py, rust/crates/saans-sim/src/scene.rs).

This schema is for external tooling. The repository's own loaders validate by hand so that no package has to be installed, and they check things a schema cannot: that objects and nodes are inside the room, that no two nodes share a point, that a polygon's bounding box matches the stated width and depth.

schema_version.description: Exactly 1 for this revision. A loader that does not know a version must refuse the file rather than guess at it; a changed meaning for an existing field is what the version exists to catch.

name.description: Short human name for the scene, e.g. 'Bedroom, 4.2 x 3.6 m'.

description.description: Free text. Say where the dimensions came from (tape measure, floor plan, RoomPlan scan) and how confident they are.

walls.description: Wall segments in plan view. A plain rectangular room needs none: the bounds are room.width_m x room.depth_m either way. List them when the materials differ wall to wall, when there are interior walls, or when a 3-D view should draw real thickness.

objects.description: Furniture and openings, as upright boxes.

nodes.description: ESP32 sensor nodes at surveyed positions. Positions are an input to localization, never an output of it: nothing in this project can self-locate a node (NOTES-localize.md §1).

people.description: Optional initial positions for simulated people. SIM data, not a measurement, and not part of the room.

phone.description: Optional initial position for the one tracked mobile phone.

point2.description: [x, y] in metres on the floor plan.

point3.description: [x, y, z] in metres; z is elevation above the floor.

wall_material.description: Wall materials, each with ITU-R P.2040 Table 3 coefficients in scenes/materials.json.

object_material.description: Furniture materials. 'fabric' has no ITU-R P.2040 entry and carries no electrical constants; it is a label for the viewer only (scenes/materials.json).

room.description: The floor plan's bounds. width_m x depth_m is the footprint; height_m is floor-to-ceiling.

depth_m.description: Extent along y, the second horizontal axis. Maps to wifisense.localize.geometry.Room.height_m.

height_m.description: Floor to ceiling, i.e. ELEVATION. The 2-D localization types have no field for this and drop it.

polygon_m.description: Floor outline for a non-rectangular room, counter-clockwise, first vertex not repeated at the end. Its bounding box must be [0, width_m] x [0, depth_m]: width_m and depth_m stay the authority on the bounds so a reader who ignores the polygon still gets the right extent.

thickness_m.description: Full thickness, centred on the segment. room.width_m x room.depth_m is the CLEAR INTERIOR floor, so a perimeter wall's centreline runs along the boundary and a viewer should draw its thickness outwards rather than eat into the floor. For an interior partition there is no outward side and the slab is symmetric about the segment.

height_m.description: Elevation of the wall top. Defaults to room.height_m when absent.

object.description: An upright box. size_m is [width, depth, height] in the object's own frame before rotation_deg is applied about the vertical axis.

type.description: 'almirah' is a free-standing wardrobe. 'door' and 'window' are openings drawn inside the wall they sit in.

centre_m.description: Centre of the box, including in z: a 2.05 m door sits at z = 1.025, not 0.

size_m.description: [width, depth, height] in metres, all positive. A double bed is about 1.9 x 1.4 m, a single about 1.9 x 0.9 m, an interior door about 0.8 m wide.

rotation_deg.description: Counter-clockwise about the vertical axis, 0 when width runs along x. Defaults to 0.

id.description: 0-255 so it fits the u8 node id the wire format and the simulator already use.

label.description: Where it physically is, e.g. 'above the door frame'.

person.description: Plan view only: the sensing stack is 2-D and assumes chests at a common height (wifisense/localize/geometry.py).

height_m.description: Standing height, for drawing only. Defaults to 1.7.

phone.description: The one tracked handset. It has a z because a phone in a pocket and a phone on a table are at different heights; the 2-D estimators ignore it.
